data.title: AI | New US Chip Rules Targeting China Pose Risks for Southeast Asia
data.description: New US rules on AI chips targeting China threaten pain for Southeast Asia, where China-linked operators are estimated to account for a significant part of data-center capacity across the region, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Crypto Rover Says Bitcoin Is Testing 300- and 350-Week Averages, a Historical Bottoming Zone
data.description: According to ChainCatcher, Crypto Rover said Bitcoin is testing its 300-week and 350-week moving averages, which he described as a historical buying zone and long-term support during deep corrections. Bitcoin found support near these levels in 2015, 2020 and 2022 before rallying significantly. Rover added that despite current market fear, history suggests the zone has offered opportunities for long-term accumulation.

data.title: Bitcoin Long Liquidation Cluster Between $59,000 and $62,000 Cleared
data.description: A dense cluster of Bitcoin long liquidations between $59,000 and $62,000 was completely cleared yesterday. According to Odaily, Glassnode said it had been tracking the cluster and that its removal eliminated a major source of forced selling below Bitcoin’s price.

data.title: FBI Investigates Suspected Hack of Criminal Information Database
data.description: According to CNBC, the FBI is investigating a suspected breach of the National Crime Information Center, a nationwide database used by federal, state and local law enforcement agencies to share criminal justice information. CNN reported Friday, citing two people briefed on the investigation, that the database was apparently compromised. It stores and shares information on warrants, criminal histories and background checks.

data.title: LART Raises $2.5 Million in Funding With IBC Group and Others Participating
data.description: According to ChainCatcher, LART, an art-recovery and RWA tokenization protocol, has completed a $2.5 million funding round, with participation from IBC Group, x21 Digital, Genesis Capital VC, and GaeaVentures. Built on BNB Smart Chain, the protocol aims to recover lost artworks, record their provenance on-chain, and bring physical art into a regulated RWA framework.

data.title: BNK Says Memory Demand Has Peaked, SK hynix Shares Are Not Undervalued
data.description: Citrini analyst Jukan said on X that a recent BNK Investment & Securities report concluded memory demand had peaked and SK hynix shares were not undervalued even at their current price. According to Odaily, BNK became the first Korean sell-side firm to downgrade SK hynix from Buy to Hold in late April, and the report effectively assigned a Sell view to the memory industry.

data.title: EU Proposes Further Cuts to Next Seven-Year Budget to Secure Deal
data.description: The European Union proposed reducing its next seven-year budget from earlier versions to help reach agreement on the package by year-end, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Global MPC Completes $7.5 Million Strategic Financing With MH Ventures Among Investors
data.description:
Global MPC, a mining RWA infrastructure project on BNB Chain, has completed $7.5 million in strategic financing, with MH Ventures, Mapleblock Capital, Paul Taylor, Genesis Capital VC, Becker Ventures, Titans Ventures and Asva Capital participating.

According to Odaily, Global MPC develops blockchain infrastructure to convert real-world mining resources into on-chain digital assets for recording and transferring those assets.

data.title: Bonkguy Holds 20x Leveraged BTC Long With Liquidation Price of $55,823
data.description: Trader Bonkguy is holding a 20x leveraged long position in BTC, with a liquidation price of $55,823. According to Odaily, the position is worth about $88,260, backed by approximately $4,325.72 in margin, with an average entry price of $58,000.

data.title: CryptoD Prefers Staying Out of Downtrends While Waiting for Clearer Market Opportunities
data.description:
Crypto trader CryptoD said they prefer to stay on the sidelines during downtrends and wait for clearer market opportunities. According to Odaily, BTC fell below $60,000, the S&P 500 dropped 3.7% in a single day, global technology stocks broadly retreated, Taiwan’s stock market fell from about 50,000 points to above 30,000, and gold hit a 14-month low.

CryptoD said limited global liquidity has made the broader market difficult to trade, while meme coins are even more challenging. In previous market cycles, capital typically flowed first into BTC, then major altcoins, and finally meme coins; CryptoD said funds are now limited and interest in meme coins has declined.

CryptoD added that most of their past profits came during periods of ample liquidity. During downtrends, they prefer to remain out of the market and wait for clearer opportunities.

data.title: Trump Again Criticizes High Interest Rates as Fed Chair Kevin Warsh Faces a Dilemma
data.description:
U.S. President Donald Trump again criticized the Federal Reserve, saying interest rates are too high and its decisions are political in nature. According to Odaily, Trump said he was not blaming Fed Chair Kevin Warsh for the remarks.

Analysts say Warsh, whom Trump nominated, faces competing pressures: Trump wants lower rates to boost markets and ease debt-servicing costs, while persistently high inflation has made the Fed reluctant to cut rates quickly. Warsh must balance the White House’s political demands with the central bank’s monetary policy independence.

data.title: Kobeissi Letter Calls AI Rout a Correction, Not a Popped Bubble
data.description:
US stocks have lost an average of $225 billion of market value a day for 31 consecutive sessions, and $6 trillion since the S&P 500 last set a record on Oct. 6. The Kobeissi Letter argues in a new note that the move is a normal correction rather than the deflation of an AI bubble.

The research letter points to capital spending as the trigger. Combined capex at Amazon, Alphabet, Meta and Microsoft rose $36.9 billion in the third quarter to a record $201.9 billion, more than double the level of a year earlier and up 356% since the first quarter of 2024. Big Tech has spent $1.6 trillion over three years, and investors have started asking when the returns arrive.

Earnings have held up. S&P 500 companies have reported 31.9% year-on-year EPS growth for the third quarter, the strongest in at least four years, and have beaten estimates for 13 consecutive quarters.

Politics explains another leg of the drop, in the letter's view. It argues the Democratic sweep in the midterms ended what it calls the "Trump Put" — the assumption that the president would step in when markets fell — and that investors now price aggressive AI regulation and even a ban once Democrats take control in January 2027. It calls those fears overdone, on the grounds that a US ban would hand the AI race to China.

The Fed adds pressure. Chair Warsh has made 2% inflation his priority, US inflation has been above target for 67 straight months and the Iran war is nearing its 300th day. Investment-grade bond sales are expected to reach $175 billion in November, up 27% from a year earlier and the highest for that month on record.

Anthropic's IPO drained liquidity at the worst moment. Institutional demand reached $400 billion and retail orders $100 billion, nearly eight times the $64.4 billion the company initially sought at $78 a share.

In chips, Nvidia has fallen 40% in a matter of weeks after the board removed Jensen Huang, and a Nov. 19 short-seller report accused AMD of smuggling chips into China, a claim the letter describes as far from substantiated. Tech's forward price-to-earnings ratio is the lowest since March 2020, and Nvidia trades at 9x, which the letter reads as the market refusing to believe its guidance of roughly $750 billion in fiscal 2028 revenue.

Sentiment gauges are at extremes. The VIX is up more than 100% from its October low and posted its biggest one-day gain since February 2018 on Nov. 5, while hedge funds recorded their largest six-week net outflow from tech in more than a decade.

The letter stops short of calling a bottom, warning that volatility will stay elevated and further losses are possible. It says another 10% decline would still leave the S&P 500 inside the range of a healthy correction, and pushes back on the 30%-plus drop forecasts now circulating. Sustained higher rates, aggressive regulation, weak AI returns and uncertainty around major companies are already in the price, it argues, leaving room for positive surprises. Once liquidity returns, it expects dip buyers to move back into quality tech, as they did in April 2025.

data.title: ETH Break Above $1,724 Could Trigger $688M in Short Liquidations on Major CEXs
data.description: According to ChainCatcher citing Coinglass data, a rise in ETH above $1,724 would bring the cumulative short liquidation intensity on major centralized exchanges to $688 million. If ETH falls below $1,563, cumulative long liquidation intensity on those exchanges would reach $435 million.

data.title: Goldman's Panic Index Hits 9 Out of 10 as Desk Sees More Selling Ahead
data.description:
Goldman Sachs' panic gauge climbed close to its maximum as U.S. stocks tumbled Friday, a signal from the bank's traders that another substantial round of selling is likely in the coming week, Bloomberg reported.

The Panic Index rose to 9 out of 10, with the retreat now spanning systematic investors. Commodity trading advisers have sold $57 billion of equities over the past month and their net positioning in U.S. stocks has flipped short by $19 billion, according to Goldman estimates. The bank's models project CTAs could offload another $65.8 billion in a flat market, $28.6 billion if stocks rise, and as much as $80.6 billion if equities keep falling.

Many investors had counted on Anthropic's record listing to revive risk appetite. Instead it failed to deliver the market-wide lift. Traders wrote that the market was looking for the world's biggest offering "to act as a clearing event to usher a 'risk-back-on' trade into year end. Without this force it has been a tough pill to swallow."

Falling prices risk feeding on themselves, because trend-following strategies cut exposure as direction and volatility shift. Questions about whether the spending on AI infrastructure, chips and computing capacity can justify sector valuations have grown louder, compounded by the turmoil at Nvidia that ended Jensen Huang's tenure.

Crowded positioning and momentum strategies have amplified the swings. The Nasdaq 100 fell 5.6% Friday for its worst week since March 2020, and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped 11%, dragged down by Nvidia, which lost 14% Friday and is down nearly 50% from its Oct. 6 peak.

The damage reached beyond institutional portfolios. Goldman's basket of retail favourites fell 8.9% and its bitcoin-sensitive basket 11%, while its cyclical-versus-defensive basket slipped 3.2% as money moved into defensives.

data.title: Japan’s Economy Contracted Slightly in Third Quarter as Rainfall Hurt Spending
data.description: Japan’s economy shrank slightly in the third quarter as a record stretch of rainfall from late August weighed on consumer spending, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Fluidkey Restores Wallet Service After Attack, Requires App Update
data.description: According to ChainCatcher, Fluidkey said its wallet service has been restored and users must update to v1.79.22 to resume transactions. The project said an attacker exploited a vulnerability in a third-party logging tool to obtain session data and prepare unauthorized transfers.

data.title: Binance Advises Users to Verify URLs Before Logging In
data.description: Binance announced on X that users should double-check a website’s URL before logging in and use Binance’s official verification tool if they are unsure.

data.title: Jiang Zhuoer Says Crypto Bear Market Is Not Over, Market Needs at Least 2 to 3 Months to Bottom
data.description:
On November 21, Jiang Zhuoer, founder of Lebit Mining Pool, said Bitcoin had fallen well below his previous estimate of $57,800 for the bear market low on July 1. According to PANews, Jiang said this indicated the bear market was not over and that investors should not expect a V-shaped recovery or a quick return to a bull market.

Jiang said the market would need at least two to three months of bottoming before the transition between bull and bear market conditions was complete, and advised against rushing to buy the dip. He added that U.S. stocks had entered a technical bear market, and said the worst-case scenario could include another leg down in the crypto bear market.

Jiang also said he had previously used cycle patterns to calculate a forecast for Bitcoin’s lowest point in the current bear market, before a rise on August 19.

data.title: ECB Invites Industry Groups to Test Tokenized Deposits and Securities
data.description: The European Central Bank (ECB) is seeking financial market participants to help explore tokenized deposits and securities through experiments supporting a blockchain-based European financial ecosystem. According to Cointelegraph, the ECB invited industry groups on Friday to join analytical work and experiments under its Appia initiative, which has three priority areas: tokenized deposits and related payments, tokenized securities, and shared network governance. Applicants must apply as collective initiatives made up of independent legal entities, rather than as individual organizations. Groups may propose work in one or more areas, and the ECB will assess applications based on expertise, practical experience, technical readiness, and expected contributions. Applications for the first experimental exercises are due by Dec. 11, with later submissions assessed on a rolling basis. The invitation is part of the Eurosystem’s broader Appia roadmap to develop a unified European tokenized financial ecosystem anchored in central bank money. The ECB plans to publish a blueprint outlining its findings and a proposed framework in 2028. ECB President Christine Lagarde has warned that Europe could miss the opportunity to establish an integrated market for tokenized securities if incompatible standards develop across platforms. She has urged policymakers to set common rules to prevent fragmentation as blockchain-based financial infrastructure advances across the region.

data.title: GMGN.Ai Co-Founder Haze Says Investors Need Not Buy at the Bottom to Capture Crypto Cycles
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher, GMGN.Ai co-founder Haze said the crypto market has again entered a “death” phase, a mood he has seen repeatedly since entering the market in 2017. He said claims that crypto is finished often come with attempts to explain price moves, but no major asset rises or falls indefinitely.

Haze described such periods as opportunities for cycle investors and secondary-market traders seeking excess returns. His approach is to buy when assets are cheap and wait for prices to rise, then sell when people focus on explaining gains, stop caring about price and assume it will keep reaching new highs. Investors may not buy at the bottom or sell at the top, he said, but can still profit.

Haze added that he was sharing a market observation, not offering investment advice or endorsing the value of any asset.
